title: New Zealand Wool for Custom Rugs: A Buyer's Guide
summary: What New Zealand wool is, why designers and hospitality buyers commonly consider it, and how it is used in custom hand-knotted and hand-tufted rugs made to order in Bhadohi.

seo.description: A buyer's guide to New Zealand wool for custom carpets and rugs: characteristics, common applications and how it is used in made-to-order production. Capability-based guidance from TAPIS GLOBAL.

definitions.definition: A premium natural protein fibre prized for bright, even colour take-up, a soft-yet-resilient hand-feel and natural durability — commonly positioned at the luxury tier for hand-knotted and hand-tufted rugs.

body.body: New Zealand wool is a natural protein fibre commonly valued for clean, even colour take-up and a soft hand-feel. In the rug trade it is often positioned at the premium-to-luxury tier and is a popular choice for hand-knotted and hand-tufted pieces.

Designers and hospitality procurement teams often consider New Zealand wool where a refined appearance and a wide, faithful colour range matter. As a natural fibre it suits made-to-order projects where colour and design are developed to a specific brief and approved via a colour sample (lab-dip) before production.

body.h2: How it is used in custom rugs
body.body: At TAPIS GLOBAL, rugs are manufactured to order in Bhadohi to the buyer's design, size, colours, construction and quantity. New Zealand wool can be specified across constructions such as hand-knotted and hand-tufted. The team confirms suitability for a specific setting and use as part of the quotation.

faq.q: Is New Zealand wool suitable for my project?
faq.a: It is commonly considered for premium residential and hospitality rugs. The TAPIS GLOBAL team can confirm suitability for your specific setting and use.

faq.q: Can you match a specific colour in wool?
faq.a: Yes — custom colours are developed to your brief and confirmed with a colour sample (lab-dip) before production.

faq.q: What does a wool rug cost?
faq.a: Cost depends on fibre grade, construction, density, size, colours, design complexity and quantity. The team prepares a quotation to your specification.
